peak_days: Swathi Nakshatram (Monthly birth star of Lord Narasimha)
festival_crowds: Annual Brahmotsavams: During this 11-day festival (February/March), over 1-2 lakh devotees visit daily. Regular daily private sevas are suspended, and additional queue complex compartments are opened.

Swathi Nakshatram: The birth star of Lord Narasimha occurs monthly, causing a massive surge of over 50,000 pilgrims. Pilgrims are advised to book accommodation and special entry tickets at least one week in advance.
Vaikuntha Ekadashi & Narasimha Jayanti: Massive congregations gather for the Uttara Dwara Darshanam (Vaikuntha Ekadashi) and dusk prayers (Narasimha Jayanti).
tips: General free darshan waiting times vary from 1 hour on weekdays to 5–8 hours during weekends and festivals. VIP Break Darshan waiting time is typically under 30–45 minutes.
Pilgrims are advised to book accommodation and special entry tickets at least one week in advance during Swathi Nakshatram.

Devotees must park their private cars at the massive multi-level parking lot at the foothills. Hilltop parking is charged at a steep fee of ₹500 per vehicle covering only the first one hour, with an additional ₹100 for every extra hour.
During massive festival crowd spikes (like the Brahmotsavams), private vehicles are often completely barred from going up, regardless of willingness to pay.
Free non-stop shuttle buses transport pilgrims from foothill parking bays and main bus stand to hilltop temple complex.
Devotees must remain within designated queue corridors and avoid pushing or jumping barricades.
Monsoon Precautions: Heavy rainfall can make the hilltop stone walkways slippery. Devotees are advised to wear rubber-soled footwear and follow instructions from security guards.

Heat Precautions during Summer: Black granite absorbs intense heat during summer months (April to June), with stone temperatures exceeding 42°C. Pilgrims are advised to wear thick socks and visit during early morning or late evening hours.
